assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions upstream/downstream directions but does not explain distance versus displacement or reference points. It does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
How does a river current affect a boat?

Going downstream, the water's speed adds to the boat, making it faster! Going upstream, it subtracts, making the boat slower. That is why it is easier to sail downstream!
copy.tl:
Paano nakakaapekto ang agos ng ilog sa bangka?

Pababa sa agos, dumaragdag ang bilis ng tubig sa bangka kaya mas mabilis ito! Pasalunga naman, nababawasan kaya mas mabagal. Kaya mas madaling sumalunong pababa kaysa pasalunga!
copy.bis:
Unsaon pag-apekto sa sulog sa suba sa bangka?

Padulong sa ubos, madugang ang katulin sa tubig sa bangka busa mas paspas kini! Padulong sa taas, makuhaan busa mas hinay. Mao nga mas sayon ang paglawig padulong sa ubos kaysa padulong sa taas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: the slower sound reaches your ears later
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions sound arriving later but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred, which is the core of G3-F-4. It only compares speeds.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The flash reaches your eyes first
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe sources of light and their use in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card references light as a flash but does not describe sources of light or their everyday uses, which is the focus of G3-F-5. It is about relative speed, not light sources.

copy.en:
Why do we see fireworks before hearing them?

Light is millions of times faster than sound! The flash reaches your eyes first, and the slower sound reaches your ears later, helping you guess how far away the fireworks are!
copy.tl:
Bakit nakikita natin ang fireworks bago marinig?

Dahil milyon-milyong beses na mas mabilis ang liwanag kaysa tunog! Nauuna ang flash sa iyong mga mata, at saka pa lang dumating ang mas mabagal na tunog. Kaya matatantya mo kung gaano kalayo ang paputok!
copy.bis:
Nganong makita una nato ang fireworks sa dili pa madungog?

Tungod kay minilyon ka beses nga mas paspas ang kahayag kaysa tingog! Moabot una ang flash sa imong mga mata, ug unya pa moabot ang mas hinay nga tingog. Mao nga matantya nimo kung unsa kalayo ang paputok!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a bus, your speed is 0 compared to your seatmate, but 60 km/h compared to the road.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure and describe changes in the position of people or objects in relation to their original position, such as moving closer, farther, left, or right
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses relative speed using different reference points, but does not involve measuring or describing changes in position relative to an original position (closer, farther, left, right). It shares the motion topic but does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: In a bus, your speed is 0 compared to your seatmate, but 60 km/h compared to the road.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the difference between distance and displacement in everyday situations in relation to a reference point
assignedReviews.reason: The card addresses the idea of comparing motion to a reference point, but it focuses on speed being relative, not on explaining the difference between distance and displacement. It does not teach distance versus displacement, so it is only related to the reference-point concept.

copy.en:
Are you moving right now?

It depends! In a bus, your speed is 0 compared to your seatmate, but 60 km/h compared to the road. Even sitting still, you spin fast with the Earth! Speed is always relative.
copy.tl:
Gumagalaw ka ba ngayon?

Nakadepende! Sa loob ng bus, 0 ang bilis mo kumpara sa katabi mo, pero 60 km/h kumpara sa kalsada. Kahit nakaupo ka lang, umiikot ka nang mabilis kasabay ng Earth! Ang bilis ay laging relative.
copy.bis:
Naglihok ba ka karon?

Nagdepende! Sulod sa bus, 0 ang imong katulin kumpara sa imong kasikbit, apan 60 km/h kumpara sa dalan. Bisan naglingkod ka lang, naglibot ka nga paspas uban sa Yuta! Ang katulin kanunay nga relative.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: faster spins mean a higher speed shown on the dashboard
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card explains how a speedometer senses wheel spin to display speed, but it does not define speed as distance per unit time. It never mentions distance or time, so it does not directly support the competency's core concept.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It senses how fast your wheels spin!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: measure accurately the distance and time when things move using simple equipment
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a speedometer's mechanism, not the act of measuring distance and time with simple equipment. No distance or time measurement is involved, so it does not support this competency.

copy.en:
How does a speedometer know how fast you're going?

It senses how fast your wheels spin! Since the machine knows the wheel's size, faster spins mean a higher speed shown on the dashboard.
copy.tl:
Paano nalalaman ng speedometer kung gaano ka kabilis?

Sinusubaybayan nito kung gaano kabilis umiikot ang gulong! Dahil alam ng makina ang sukat ng gulong, mas mabilis na ikot ay mas mataas na speed ang ipinapakita.
copy.bis:
Unsaon pagsabot sa speedometer kung unsa ka paspas ka?

Gibantayan niini kung unsa ka paspas ang paglibot sa ligid! Tungod kay nahibalo ang makina sa gidak-on sa ligid, mas paspas nga paglibot mas taas nga speed ang ipakita.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The faster a car goes, the longer its stopping distance!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided activities to demonstrate that pushes and pulls can be used to change the speed and direction of an object including making it go faster, turn it to a different direction, slow it down, and stop it
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses stopping distance in relation to speed but does not demonstrate that pushes or pulls change speed or direction. It does not mention forces, braking, or any guided activity involving pushes/pulls.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The faster a car goes, the longer its stopping distance!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify that how far an object moves in a given time is called speed
assignedReviews.reason: The card uses the concept of speed but does not define speed as distance over time. It focuses on the relationship between speed and stopping distance, not on identifying what speed is.

copy.en: The faster a car goes, the longer its stopping distance! If you double the speed, the stopping distance grows even more than double. That is why speeding is so dangerous!
copy.tl: Kapag mas mabilis ang sasakyan, mas mahaba ang stopping distance! Kapag dinoble mo ang bilis, mas mahaba pa sa doble ang kailangan nitong layo para huminto. Kaya delikado ang sobrang bilis!
copy.bis: Kung mas paspas ang sakyanan, mas taas ang stopping distance! Kung doblehon nimo ang katulin, mas taas pa sa doble ang gilay-on nga gikinahanglan niini sa paghunong. Mao nga delikado ang sobra ka paspas!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The vas deferens is the tube that carries sperm
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: participate in guided science activities to explore and describe sources of light, how it behaves or can be changed, and its uses in everyday situations
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the male reproductive system (vas deferens, testes, urethra), which is unrelated to the competency about exploring sources of light, its behavior, and uses. The content does not support any part of G3-F-6.

copy.en: The vas deferens is the tube that carries sperm from the testes to the urethra, working like the fallopian tube does in females.
copy.tl: Ang vas deferens ay ang tubong nagdadala ng sperm mula sa testes papunta sa urethra, katulad ng ginagawa ng fallopian tube sa mga babae.
copy.bis: Ang vas deferens mao ang tubo nga nagdala sa sperm gikan sa testes ngadto sa urethra, sama sa gibuhat sa fallopian tube sa mga baye.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: breathes through a blowhole on top of its head
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an outer body part (blowhole) but does not describe its role in movement or gathering food, which is the focus of G3-L-4.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: breathes through a blowhole on top of its head
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the respiratory system as the nose, windpipe, and lungs, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions breathing but does not identify or describe the respiratory system parts (nose, windpipe, lungs) or how they work, as required by G5-L-2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: so it must surface for air
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card implies the need for air, but does not identify basic needs of all living things (air, food, water, shelter) or teach the concept of basic needs directly.

copy.en: The sperm whale breathes through a blowhole on top of its head, so it must surface for air!
copy.tl: Humihinga ang sperm whale sa butas sa tuktok ng ulo nito na tinatawag na blowhole, kaya kailangan nitong umahon para huminga!
copy.bis: Moginhawa ang sperm whale sa lungag sa ibabaw sa ulo niini nga gitawag og blowhole, mao nga kinahanglan kini mosaka aron makaginhawa!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sperm whale's click is one of the loudest sounds any animal on Earth can make
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and identify sources and uses of light, sound, and heat energy at school, at home and in the local community
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions a sound source (sperm whale click) but does not address identifying sources and uses of sound energy at school, home, or in the local community. It is only about a natural sound's loudness, not its source/use in everyday settings.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The sperm whale's click is one of the loudest sounds any animal on Earth can make
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explore and describe how sound is made and transferred in everyday situations, such as the ringing of a bell or the hearing of noises
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a loud sound but does not explore or describe how sound is made or transferred in everyday situations. It provides no mechanism of sound production or transfer, only a comparative loudness fact.

copy.en: The sperm whale's click is one of the loudest sounds any animal on Earth can make — even louder than a jet plane!
copy.tl: Ang click ng sperm whale ay isa sa pinakamalalakas na tunog na nagagawa ng kahit anong hayop sa mundo — mas malakas pa kaysa eroplano!
copy.bis: Ang click sa sperm whale usa sa pinakakusog nga tingog nga mahimo sa bisan unsang hayop sa kalibutan — mas kusog pa kaysa eroplano!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: spices like garlic, chili, and pepper also slow down germs, helping keep some foods from spoiling quickly
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: explain the factors affecting the rates of chemical reactions as applied in food preservation and materials production, control of fire, pollution, and corrosion
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses food preservation via antimicrobial properties of spices, but does not explain any factor affecting the rate of a chemical reaction (e.g., temperature, concentration, surface area, catalyst). It only mentions slowing germs, which is not a chemical reaction rate concept. Thus it is related to the food preservation application but does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Do spices only add flavor to food?

No — spices like garlic, chili, and pepper also slow down germs, helping keep some foods from spoiling quickly.
copy.tl:
Panlasa lang ba ang dulot ng pampalasa?

Hindi lang! Ang bawang, sili, at paminta ay nakakatulong ding pigilan ang ilang mikrobyo, kaya hindi madaling masira ang ilang pagkain.
copy.bis:
Lami ra ba ang gihatag sa panakot?

Dili lang! Ang ahos, sili, ug paminta motabang usab pagpugong sa ubang mikrobyo, mao nga dili dali madaot ang ubang pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: It actually comes from the tip of the belly, not the mouth!
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes the belly as the source of spider silk, but the competency requires identifying outer body parts and their role in movement and gathering food. Silk production is not movement or food gathering, so the card does not directly support the competency.

copy.en:
Where does spider silk come from?

It actually comes from the tip of the belly, not the mouth!
copy.tl:
Saan nanggagaling ang sutla ng gagamba?

Lumalabas pala ito sa dulo ng tiyan, hindi sa bibig!
copy.bis:
Asa gikan ang seda sa lawalawa?

Gikan diay kini sa tumoy sa tiyan, dili sa baba!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: thin draglines on walls and ceilings that shine when light hits them
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the physical properties of solid materials, such as hard, shiny, or stretchable
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes spider draglines that shine, which is a shiny property of a solid material. However, the competency asks students to describe physical properties of solid materials generally (hard, shiny, stretchable). The card does not frame the dragline as a solid material nor teach the concept of physical properties; it merely states an observation about a spider product. This is background/related content, not direct instruction for the competency.

copy.en: House spiders in the Philippines often leave thin draglines on walls and ceilings that shine when light hits them.
copy.tl: Ang mga gagambang nakatira sa bahay ay madalas nag-iiwan ng manipis na sinulid sa dingding at kisame na kumikinang kapag tinamaan ng liwanag.
copy.bis: Ang mga lawalawa sa balay kanunay magbilin og nipis nga hilo sa bungbong ug kisame nga mokidlap kon masidlakan og suga.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The spin quantum number, written as ms, describes how an electron spins on its own axis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: draw the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells
assignedReviews.reason: The card discusses electron spin, a quantum property, but does not support drawing the structure of an atom in terms of the nucleus and electron shells.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: The spin quantum number, written as ms, describes how an electron spins on its own axis
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: differentiate the subatomic particles protons, neutrons, and electrons in terms of their symbol, mass, charge, and location within an atom
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions an electron property but does not differentiate protons, neutrons, and electrons by symbol, mass, charge, or location within an atom.

copy.en:
Why do two electrons in the same orbital have different arrows in diagrams?

They have different spin quantum numbers, ms! One electron spins upward with ms = +1/2, and the other spins downward with ms = -1/2.
copy.tl:
Bakit magkaiba ang mga arrow ng dalawang electron sa parehong orbital sa mga diagram?

Magkaiba ang kanilang spin quantum numbers, ms! Ang isang electron ay umiikot pataas na may ms = +1/2, at ang isa ay umiikot pababa na may ms = -1/2.
copy.bis:
Ngano nga lahi ang mga arrow sa duha ka electron sa parehong orbital sa mga diagram?

Lahi ang ilang spin quantum numbers, ms! Ang usa ka electron moliko pataas nga adunay ms = +1/2, ug ang usa moliko paubos nga adunay ms = -1/2.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A baby is born with 33 vertebrae in the spine, but some fuse together over time, leaving an adult with only about 26.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: The card gives a developmental fact about the number of vertebrae in the spine, but it does not describe how the skeletal system works (e.g., support, movement, protection). It is only tangentially related to the skeletal system.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A baby is born with 33 vertebrae in the spine, but some fuse together over time, leaving an adult with only about 26.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the characteristics of living things: they grow, respond, and reproduce
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a change in the number of vertebrae as a person grows, but it does not describe the characteristics of living things (grow, respond, reproduce). The fusion of bones is not presented as growth of the organism, and no connection to the competency's core concept is made.

copy.en:
Do babies have more bones in their spine?

A baby is born with 33 vertebrae in the spine, but some fuse together over time, leaving an adult with only about 26.
copy.tl:
Mas marami bang buto ang gulugod ng sanggol?

Ang sanggol ay ipinapanganak na may 33 vertebrae sa gulugod, pero nagsasanib ang ilan sa paglipas ng panahon kaya 26 na lamang ito sa nasa hustong gulang.
copy.bis:
Mas daghan ba og bukog ang gulugod sa masuso?

Ang masuso natawo nga adunay 33 ka vertebrae sa gulugod, apan ang uban magdugtong sa paglabay sa panahon mao nga mahimong halos 26 na lang sa hamtong.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Spinosaurus grew to about 15 meters long
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe different science process skills used in performing simple science activities, such as observing, predicting, and measuring using units such as millimeter, centimeter, and meter
assignedReviews.reason: The card states a length in meters but does not describe or teach any science process skill such as observing, predicting, or measuring. It is a factual statement about an animal's size, not instruction on measurement or process skills.

copy.en: Spinosaurus grew to about 15 meters long — even longer than the mighty Tyrannosaurus rex!
copy.tl: Umabot ang Spinosaurus sa halos 15 metro ang haba — mas mahaba pa sa Tyrannosaurus rex!
copy.bis: Miabot ang Spinosaurus sa mga 15 ka metro ang gitas-on — mas taas pa kay sa Tyrannosaurus rex!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Your spleen collects old and damaged red blood cells, removes them from your blood, and recycles some of their parts to reuse
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify from pictures and diagrams the parts of the circulatory system as heart, blood, and blood vessels, and describe how they work
assignedReviews.reason: Spleen recycling of old red cells is not identifying heart, blood, and blood vessels and how they work.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: collects old and damaged red blood cells, removes them from your blood
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe in simple terms how the following human body systems work: muscular, skeletal, digestive, circulatory, and respiratory
assignedReviews.reason: Spleen recycling is not the five body systems as a set.

copy.en:
What does your spleen do to old blood cells?

Your spleen collects old and damaged red blood cells, removes them from your blood, and recycles some of their parts to reuse.
copy.tl:
Ano ang ginagawa ng pali sa lumang dugo?

Kinokolekta ng pali ang luma at sirang pulang selula ng dugo, inaalis ito sa dugo, at muling ginagamit ang ilang bahagi nito.
copy.bis:
Unsa ang buhaton sa pali sa daan nga dugo?

Ang pali motigom sa daan ug guba nga pula nga selula sa dugo, tangtangon kini gikan sa dugo, ug gigamit pag-usab ang ubang bahin niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sponge eats by filtering tiny bits of food from the water that flows through its body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes how a sponge obtains food by filtering, but it does not identify or teach the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It only illustrates one feeding behavior, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sponge eats by filtering tiny bits of food from the water that flows through its body.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe and describe the outer body parts of animals, such as head, legs or wings, and identify their role to move and to gather food
assignedReviews.reason: The card is about feeding by filtering, not about observing or describing outer body parts of animals such as head, legs, or wings, nor their role in movement and gathering food. Sponges lack the named outer body parts, so this is only loosely related to animal body parts and food gathering.

copy.en:
How does a sponge eat?

By filtering! A sponge eats by filtering tiny bits of food from the water that flows through its body.
copy.tl:
Paano kumakain ang espongha?

Sa pagsala! Kumakain ang espongha sa pamamagitan ng pagsala ng maliliit na pagkain mula sa tubig na dumadaloy sa katawan nito.
copy.bis:
Giunsa pagkaon sa espongha?

Pinaagi sa pagsala! Mokaon ang espongha pinaagi sa pagsala sa gagmay nga pagkaon gikan sa tubig nga moagi sa lawas niini.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: Sponges are the simplest animals with many cells — they have no brain, heart, or muscles
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: Calling a sponge the simplest many-celled animal is not recognizing unicellular versus multicellular organisms.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: they have no brain, heart, or muscles. They just pull water through thousands of tiny pores to filter out food
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: describe the differences between animals with a backbone (vertebrates) and animals without backbones (invertebrates) by using common local examples of each group
assignedReviews.reason: A brainless filter-feeder is an invertebrate example, but the card does not describe backbone versus no backbone.

copy.en:
Why is the sponge called the simplest animal?

Sponges are the simplest animals with many cells — they have no brain, heart, or muscles. They just pull water through thousands of tiny pores to filter out food.
copy.tl:
Bakit tinatawag na pinaka-simpleng hayop ang esponghas?

Ang esponghas ang pinaka-simpleng multicellular na hayop — walang utak, puso, o kalamnan. Dumadaan lang ang tubig sa libu-libong maliliit na butas nito para sumala ng pagkain.
copy.bis:
Nganong gitawag nga pinaka-simple nga hayop ang esponghas?

Ang esponghas mao ang pinaka-simple nga multicellular nga hayop — walay utok, kasingkasing, o kaunoran. Moagi lang ang tubig sa liboan ka gagmayng lungag niini aron mosala og pagkaon.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sponge can filter more than ten times its own volume of water every hour, using thousands of tiny cells to remove bacteria and particles.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sponge's water-filtering ability, not the basic needs of living things such as air, food, water, and shelter. It shares the broad living-things topic but does not directly support identifying basic needs.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A sponge can filter more than ten times its own volume of water every hour, using thousands of tiny cells to remove bacteria and particles.
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: recognize that some organisms consist of a single cell (unicellular) like in bacteria and some consist of many cells (multicellular) like in a human
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions that a sponge uses thousands of tiny cells, which implies multicellularity, but it does not teach the contrast between unicellular organisms like bacteria and multicellular organisms like humans. It does not directly support recognizing the unicellular/multicellular distinction.

copy.en:
How much water can a sponge filter?

A sponge can filter more than ten times its own volume of water every hour, using thousands of tiny cells to remove bacteria and particles.
copy.tl:
Gaano karaming tubig ang na-filter ng sponge?

Kayang i-filter ng isang espongha ang higit sa sampung beses ng sarili nitong dami ng tubig kada oras, gamit ang libu-libong maliit na selula.
copy.bis:
Pila ka daghan ang tubig nga ma-filter sa espongha?

Ang usa ka espongha makahimo og pag-filter labaw sa napulo ka beses sa iyang kaugalingong gidak-on sa tubig matag oras, gamit ang liboan ka gamay nga selula.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A single sponge can filter through a huge amount of water every day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sponge's filtering capacity, not the basic needs of living things (air, food, water, shelter). It does not teach that water is a basic need or identify any basic need.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: A single sponge can filter through a huge amount of water every day
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card does not show how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs. It only states a sponge filters water, with no dependency or environment connection.

copy.en:
How much water can a sponge filter?

A single sponge can filter through a huge amount of water every day — way more than its own size!
copy.tl:
Gaano kadaming tubig ang nasasala ng espongha?

Kaya ng isang espongha na salain ang napakaraming tubig bawat araw — mas marami pa kaysa sa sarili nitong laki!
copy.bis:
Pila ka tubig ang masala sa espongha?

Ang usa ka espongha makasala og daghan kaayong tubig matag adlaw — mas daghan pa kay sa iyang kaugalingong gidak-on!

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it takes oxygen straight from the water flowing through its body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: identify the basic needs of all living things, such as air, food, water, and shelter
assignedReviews.reason: The card mentions oxygen (air) and water, which are basic needs, but it does not identify or teach the concept of basic needs of all living things. It only describes how a sponge obtains oxygen, so it does not directly support the competency.

assignedReviews.card_evidence: it takes oxygen straight from the water flowing through its body
assignedReviews.competency_evidence: observe examples and explain how living things depend on one another and on the environment to meet their basic needs
assignedReviews.reason: The card describes a sponge getting oxygen from its environment (water), which touches on dependence on the environment, but it does not explain how living things depend on one another or on the environment to meet basic needs in a general sense. It is a specific example without the explanatory link required by the competency.

copy.en:
How does a sponge breathe?

A sponge has no lungs at all, it takes oxygen straight from the water flowing through its body.
copy.tl:
Paano humihinga ang espongha?

Wala talagang baga ang espongha, kumukuha ito ng oksiheno mismo sa tubig na dumadaloy sa katawan nito.
copy.bis:

Why do we care about a star's color?

Stars are too far and hot to visit! But by looking at their light's color from Earth, we know their surface heat. Color is our space 'thermometer'!

Sobrang layo at init para bisitahin! Pero sa pagtingin sa kulay ng liwanag nito mula Earth, alam na natin ang init ng ibabaw nito. Ang kulay ang 'thermometer' natin sa kalawakan!

Proxima Centauri is about 4.2 light-years away! Even with current technology, a fast rocket would still take over 70,000 years to reach it.

Why do stars twinkle but planets don't?

Stars twinkle because their light bends through Earth's moving atmosphere layers! Planets are closer and look bigger, so they shine steadily instead of twinkling.

Bakit nagkikislap ang mga bituin pero hindi ang mga planeta?

Nagkikislap ang mga bituin dahil ang ilaw ay dumadaan sa gumagalaw na atmosphere ng Earth! Mas malapit ang mga planeta kaya sumisilip nang maayos at hindi nagkikislap.

No! A starfish has no heart and no brain at all. Instead, it uses a water system inside its body to move nutrients around.
